title: Playing blues and church songs with feeling; early pay at picture shows
summary: Slim says blues must be played with feeling, credits Little Brother, and recalls his low early pay playing at silent picture shows.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: They were singing with a feeling.

Yeah, that's what it is. It's the same thing, if you play the blues, then play it with a feeling. And, uh, if you don't play but three jazz pieces, if you're not an educated musician, play it and learn to play that with a feeling. That's why I give brother and Piara a whole more credit than I do. You know somebody can really put the right stuff to it, you see. And, uh, Piara play for rich and poor.
Well, for a person to play that good, you have to know what he's doing anyway. Yeah. See, you got to know your cause, and know what it is, and what to call it, everything. How to build, everything.

Yeah. And you don't just learn that, and, uh, just do like I do, you know. See, I jump up and play the blues. I feel that more than I do that. And when I get down to learn that, like a man, when he's talking about coming to Oliver, we sit down, used to sit down in rehearsal, hymn and crossing. Wasn't up but bass and a guitar and horn and piano. And we'd get back in a room where nobody bothered. And he said, da, this thing, da, and drop. Well, you see, I'm a fella I wouldn't forget that. But the school, I didn't have it. See, brother, brother worked hard. Brother was famished. Just famished as a man you want to be through and through. But he saw his mistakes up to the line. And he tried to add, add, read. And it, you know, it puts a wonder on you. See, but you know, I was just hollering, lying, lying, learning how to play. When I first come down home, started going down there. Down and a half here at this place, two and a half over that place. I played at the movie, movie picture show, which there wasn't no talking them times. I'd get a dollar head and go out there. Well, that's more money I done plowed on me than we left all week for, you see. That's two and a half of the dollar head. Then the girls gonna give me some whiskey and some dimes and quarters sometimes, you know. Some of the fellas win, you play something like that, they gonna like to drop their half dollars. But sometimes you leave them jack for six, seven dollars. Well, you know, what you doing? You plowed a week for four dollars.
